requirement:
For every `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a
requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced
requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover
the reference's file and line. An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone
MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. `{impl}` and `{cite}` sources
remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`;
`{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by
{cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered
reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line
number.
rationale:
I judged the marked tests adequate for `requirements.references.evidence_coverage`. I did not request implementation source. The expected behavior comes from the requirement text, and I checked it against the assertions in the supplied tests.

**Obligation 1: every `{test}` reference needs an input covering its file and line.**
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines]` writes two identical `{test}` lines in a plain-text source. The evidence input selects only the first line, so the second is uncovered. The test asserts the exact error in the form `no input covers {test}`<name>` at <file>:<line>`. It also asserts exactly two errors in total, so the covered line is not reported.
- `fn[source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs]` is the positive case. A `{test}` reference in a markdown file is covered by a line-range outline input, and a whole-file input covers the source file. The test asserts no errors.
- `fn[cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates]` covers the "including one in a requirement or example declaration" clause. A `{test}` inside a requirement or example declaration is covered by a requirements input over that declaration, and it stays covered after the declaration moves. A `{test}` outside the declaration is reported uncovered. With the inputs emptied, the in-declaration `{test}` is reported with its file and line. For the example's own evidence, an empty `inputs` array reports the `{test}` in `src/main.rs`.
- `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references]` adds a new `{test}` in `other.txt` and asserts that `no input covers` and the file and line are reported. A `{fixme}` on the same requirement does not hide the gap.

**Obligation 2: `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{fixme}` alone need no input.**
- `fn[only_test_references_require_recorded_source_coverage]` has `{cite}`, `{impl}` and `{test}` references in one source file and empty inputs. It asserts exactly one uncovered error, for the `{test}`, and no error for the `{cite}`.
- The same test selects only the test function and then changes the unread implementation body. Validation still passes, so `{impl}` needs no input.
- `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[editing_or_adding_a_fixme_makes_evidence_stale_without_requiring_source_reads]` adds a `{fixme}` in `other.rs` and asserts that no `no input covers {fixme}` error appears.
- `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_fixme_inside_a_site_belongs_to_that_sites_review_only]` asserts that `{fixme}` references inside sites produce no `no input covers {fixme}` errors.

**Obligation 3: the report names role, full name, file and line.** The exact-message assertion in `fn[reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines]` includes the role (`{test}`), the full name, the file and the line. The other tests assert the name, file and line, and the role `{test}`.

**Delegated obligations.** The `reference_index`, `fixme_inputs` and `reference_set` citations are context only. Their own tests are not reassessed here.

**Gaps.** I found none. The coverage rule's modes (source file, markdown, in-declaration, requirement and example evidence), its negative cases (impl, cite, fixme) and its reporting format are all exercised with enforcing assertions.

text: :::{req} evidence_coverage
For every `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a
requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced
requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover
the reference's file and line. An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone
MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. `{impl}` and `{cite}` sources
remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`;
`{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by
{cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered
reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line
number.
:::{req} reference_index
The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:
```text
references({ selection: String?, roles: Array<"impl" | "cite" | "test">? }) -> ReferenceIndex
ReferenceIndex {
definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }
ReferenceSite {
name: String,
role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
file: String,
item: String?,
`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
reference to any match whose role is in `roles`, defaulting to
`["impl", "cite", "test"]`, under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and position in the file, without line
numbers. Roles MUST be treated as a set: repeating a permitted role MUST NOT
duplicate sites or change the result.
An anchor under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` whose role is selected
by `roles` MUST be
reported as a site for its anchored file, with the anchored node's selector as
`item` when it names one and no `item` when it names the whole file. Every
other site MUST give as `item` the selector of its smallest enclosing outline
node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.
An empty `roles` array MUST return no sites while preserving the selected
definitions' names and kinds. An unknown role or a value other than an array of
permitted role strings MUST return an explanatory tool error. Without `selection`,
`roles` MUST NOT change the definition-name listing.
Results MUST contain no requirement text, example text, reference commentary,
or source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool. For example,
`references({selection: "requirements.cli.status", roles: ["impl"]})` MUST
locate only that subject's implementation references and anchors, without
supplying their source or recording evidence inputs.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
